chapter_summary: Proverbs 31 opens with a king's mother warning her son about the dangers of women who lead him astray, the destruction of strong drink for rulers, and the solemn call to speak up for those who cannot defend themselves. The second and longer section is a famous poem celebrating a woman of excellent character — her hard work, her generosity to the poor, her care for her family, her wisdom and kindness in speech, and her deep fear of the LORD. The chapter closes with the declaration that outward beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears God will be praised. Together, the chapter connects wise leadership, just speech, diligent labour, and reverence for God as the marks of true excellence.
main_lesson: The best thing about any person is not how they look, but how they love God and work hard to care for others.

memory_verse.kjv: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
memory_verse.little_bible: Good looks can fool you. But a woman who respects God will always be praised.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 31 is one of the most beloved chapters in all of Scripture, and it is also one of the most theologically dense. The opening verses (1–9) are often overlooked, but they carry vital wisdom for leadership. A king's mother warns him about the twin dangers of sexual immorality and drunkenness — not merely as moral failures but as destroyers of justice. A king who is led astray by either will 'forget the law and pervert the judgment of the afflicted.' The connection between personal virtue and public justice is direct. Good leaders must be personally disciplined if they are to be just.

Verses 8–9 are a call to prophetic advocacy: 'Open thy mouth for the dumb' — speak for those who cannot speak for themselves, judge righteously, plead for the poor and needy. This is not optional charity but the defining mark of just leadership. For families, this is an early lesson in using our voice and influence to protect the vulnerable.

The famous Proverbs 31 woman (vv. 10–31) is an acrostic poem in Hebrew — each verse beginning with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet. This artistic structure underscores that her excellence is complete, from A to Z. She is not a fantasy of perfection but an integrated picture of godly character: she works hard, she is generous, she is prepared, she is wise in speech, she fears God. Her praise comes not from her beauty but from her works.

For your children, the key lesson is that what we do matters more than how we look. The woman in this poem is celebrated because she gave herself to others — her family, the poor, her community. Teach your children that their hands, their words, and their choices are the things that will truly commend them. The chapter ends with a call to give her the praise she deserves: 'let her own works praise her in the gates.' True reputation is built on faithful character, not on appearances.
application_for_children: This week, look for one way to help someone at home without being asked. Work hard and be kind. That is what it means to be truly excellent.

verses.kjv: The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him.
verses.little_bible: These are the words of King Lemuel. His mother taught him this wisdom.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A mother taught her son, the king, wise things.
verses.meaning: The chapter opens with a remarkable detail: this royal wisdom comes from a mother. God works through parents to shape leaders. The word 'prophecy' here means a serious, weighty burden of instruction — this is not casual advice but vital truth passed from a faithful mother to her son the king.
verses.prayer: God, help me listen to my parents.
verses.discussion_question: Who teaches you important things about life?
verses.family_discussion: How intentional are we as parents in passing on wisdom to our children — not just by example but through direct instruction and conversation?
verses.do_it_today: Thank a parent or teacher for something wise they have taught you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A gentle mother sitting beside her young king son on a throne step, speaking quietly to him, warm candlelight, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows?
verses.little_bible: Listen, my son! You are my own dear child. I prayed for you and promised you to God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A loving mother calls out to her dear child.
verses.meaning: The mother's urgent repetition — 'what, my son?' three times — reflects deep love and earnest concern. 'Son of my vows' tells us she had dedicated this child to God in prayer. Parents who dedicate their children to God have a holy responsibility to train them in wisdom.
verses.prayer: God, I belong to You. Help me live for You.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be promised to God?
verses.family_discussion: Have you ever dedicated your child to God in prayer? How does that commitment shape the way you parent?
verses.do_it_today: Tell God you want your whole life to belong to Him.
verses.illustration_prompt: A mother kneeling in prayer holding her infant up toward the light, humble and devoted expression, soft watercolour in warm tones

verses.kjv: Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.
verses.little_bible: Do not waste your strength on the wrong things. Some choices have destroyed even kings.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not give your life to things that destroy you.
verses.meaning: The mother warns her royal son against sexual immorality. History bears her out: many kings were ruined by lust (Solomon himself, Samson, David). The warning is not against women but against sinful choices that drain a leader of God-given strength and destroy their ability to rule justly.
verses.prayer: God, help me use my strength for You.
verses.discussion_question: Why are some choices dangerous even for powerful people?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our sons understand that sexual purity is not just a personal virtue but directly tied to their capacity to lead, serve, and remain just?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one thing you want to use your strength for. Make it a good thing that honours God.
verses.illustration_prompt: A young king standing at a crossroads, one path glowing with light and purpose, the other leading into shadow, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:
verses.little_bible: Kings should not drink wine. Princes should not drink strong drink. Leaders must stay clear-headed.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Leaders must stay sharp and clear-headed.
verses.meaning: The repetition 'it is not for kings… it is not for kings' is emphatic — this is a firm boundary. Leaders carry responsibilities that require clear minds and sound judgment. Drunkenness in a leader is not merely a personal vice; it has consequences for everyone they lead.
verses.prayer: God, help leaders make wise choices.
verses.discussion_question: Why do leaders need to think especially clearly?
verses.family_discussion: What does this say about the connection between personal self-control and the ability to exercise justice for others?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a leader you respect. Pray for that person to stay wise and clear-headed.
verses.illustration_prompt: A king thoughtfully turning away from a cup of wine, looking instead toward a scroll of wisdom, watercolour illustration with warm golden light

verses.kjv: Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.
verses.little_bible: A drunk ruler forgets God's law. He gives unfair judgments to people who are suffering.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A fuzzy mind cannot give fair help to others.
verses.meaning: Here is the exact danger spelled out: a leader who drinks forgets the law and perverts judgment for the afflicted — meaning the weak, the poor, and the suffering are harmed. Personal sin has public consequences. The vulnerable are the ones who suffer most when leaders fail.
verses.prayer: God, help leaders be fair to the weak.
verses.discussion_question: How do a leader's bad choices hurt the people they lead?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children that their choices ripple outward and affect others — especially those who are weaker or depend on them?
verses.do_it_today: Think about a choice you make every day. How does that choice affect the people around you?
verses.illustration_prompt: A blurred, stumbling figure at a judge's bench while small figures below wait anxiously for justice, grey tones contrasted with the light outside, watercolour

verses.kjv: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts.
verses.little_bible: Strong drink may bring a little comfort to those who are dying. Wine may ease the pain of deep sadness.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People who are suffering greatly need special comfort.
verses.meaning: This verse is a contrast with the previous two. Whereas strong drink is forbidden for kings, it was historically permitted as a mercy for those in extreme pain or dying — a medicinal, compassionate use. The verse underscores that context matters and that the same substance that destroys a ruler's judgment may be an act of mercy for the suffering.
verses.prayer: God, help me comfort people who are hurting.
verses.discussion_question: How can we show kindness to people who are very sad?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop compassion for those in extreme suffering — going beyond sympathy to practical, sacrificial comfort?
verses.do_it_today: If you know someone who is very sad, do one kind thing for them today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A caring figure kneeling beside a grieving person in a simple room, offering comfort with a gentle hand and a cup, warm soft watercolour tones

verses.kjv: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
verses.little_bible: Let the suffering person find some relief from pain. Let them have a moment of forgetting their troubles.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People who hurt deeply need someone to bring relief.
verses.meaning: Continuing from verse 6, this verse emphasises compassion for those in desperate poverty and misery. The pastoral concern is genuine: relieving suffering is a godly impulse. The deeper lesson is that God cares about the pain of the poor and expects His people to do the same.
verses.prayer: God, help me see the hurting around me.
verses.discussion_question: What can we do when someone is very poor or sad?
verses.family_discussion: In what practical ways does your family act as an agent of relief and comfort for those in genuine poverty or misery in your community?
verses.do_it_today: Look for one person at school or at home who seems sad. Ask them if they are okay.
verses.illustration_prompt: A poor, downcast figure sitting alone finding a moment of peace as a sunset glows warmly on their face, watercolour scene in golden and soft blue tones

verses.kjv: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.
verses.little_bible: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves. Help those who are in danger.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Use your voice to help people who cannot speak for themselves.
verses.meaning: This is one of Scripture's clearest calls to advocacy. 'The dumb' means those who cannot speak — whether literally or because they have no power or voice in society. The 'appointed to destruction' are those facing unjust death or ruin. Godly people use their voice to protect the defenceless.
verses.prayer: God, help me speak up for the weak.
verses.discussion_question: Who are the people who need someone to speak for them?
verses.family_discussion: How are we raising our children to use their voice and privilege to advocate for the vulnerable — not just feel sorry for them?
verses.do_it_today: If you see someone being left out or treated unfairly today, speak up kindly on their behalf.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing up and speaking boldly while a smaller, frightened child is protected behind them, gentle light and courage in the scene, watercolour

verses.kjv: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
verses.little_bible: Speak up. Be fair and right in your judgments. Stand up for the poor and those who need help.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Be fair. Help poor and needy people.
verses.meaning: This is the climax of the first section: the summary of what a good king must do. It pairs speech ('open thy mouth'), justice ('judge righteously'), and advocacy ('plead the cause of the poor and needy'). These three are not separate; they work together. True justice speaks, acts fairly, and champions the vulnerable.
verses.prayer: God, make me someone who speaks up rightly.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to stand up for someone who needs help?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model righteous speech and just advocacy in our home — in the way we talk about those who are vulnerable, poor, or marginalised?
verses.do_it_today: Practice being fair today. If something is unfair at home or school, say something kind but honest about it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise figure standing in an open gate, speaking with authority while a crowd of small and humble figures listens with hope, watercolour illustration in warm light

verses.kjv: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
verses.little_bible: A woman of excellent character is very hard to find. She is worth more than the rarest gems.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A good and kind woman is worth more than any treasure.
verses.meaning: The famous poem begins with a rhetorical question that signals rarity and great worth. 'Virtuous' in Hebrew is the word 'chayil' — strength, excellence, capability. This is not a passive domesticity but an active, strong character. Her value exceeds rubies — the most precious gemstone of the ancient world.
verses.prayer: God, give me excellent character inside.
verses.discussion_question: What makes a person truly valuable?
verses.family_discussion: How do we counteract our culture's message that a woman's worth is in her appearance, and instead invest in building deep character in our daughters?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one woman in your life who has excellent character. Tell her why you appreciate her.
verses.illustration_prompt: A graceful woman standing tall in golden morning light, a pile of gems in the foreground far smaller than her radiant presence, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.
verses.little_bible: Her husband trusts her completely. He does not need to worry. She is enough for him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Her husband trusts her completely.
verses.meaning: Trust is foundational to a godly marriage. The husband's full confidence in his wife frees him from anxiety and removes any temptation to seek gain dishonestly ('no need of spoil'). Her faithfulness creates security. A trustworthy character is one of the greatest gifts one person can give another.
verses.prayer: God, make me someone others can trust.
verses.discussion_question: Why is being trustworthy so important in a family?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build a culture of trust in our home, where each person's word is reliable and their character is consistent?
verses.do_it_today: Do what you said you would do today. Be a person of your word.
verses.illustration_prompt: A husband and wife sitting peacefully together, an expression of deep and settled trust between them, warm home setting, gentle watercolour tones

verses.kjv: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.
verses.little_bible: Every day of her life, she chooses to do good to her husband. She never turns against him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She always does good to her husband, every single day.
verses.meaning: This is a commitment of steadfast, daily goodness — not just occasional acts of kindness but a consistent pattern over a lifetime. The phrase 'all the days of her life' speaks to faithfulness and endurance. Godly love is not situational; it persists across seasons, difficulties, and years.
verses.prayer: God, help me do good to others daily.
verses.discussion_question: How can you do good to your family every single day?
verses.family_discussion: What daily practices in our home build a habit of goodness toward one another rather than just occasional kindness?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one person at home. Do something good for them without being asked.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman placing a warm meal on the table while sunlight streams in the window, a calm and faithful home scene, gentle watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She seeketh wool and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.
verses.little_bible: She finds the best wool and linen. She works hard with her hands, and she does it gladly.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She works hard with her hands and she loves doing it.
verses.meaning: Wool and flax are the raw materials for making clothing. She is not waiting for things to appear — she seeks them out. And she works 'willingly,' not grudgingly. This is the picture of someone who finds genuine joy and dignity in diligent, productive work. Hard work done gladly is a gift from God.
verses.prayer: God, help me work hard for others.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to work willingly and not just when you have to?
verses.family_discussion: How do we instil in our children a love for diligent work rather than a tolerance for it — a sense that purposeful effort is dignifying and good?
verses.do_it_today: Do one chore at home today without complaining. Do it with a good attitude.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman happily spinning wool by a window in warm morning light, her hands busy and her expression content and purposeful, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar.
verses.little_bible: She is like a ship that travels far. She brings the best food home for her family.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She goes far to find the very best for her family.
verses.meaning: The merchant ship image conveys ambition, range, and initiative. She does not settle for the nearest or easiest option. She ranges widely to provide the best for those in her care. This is proactive, strategic provision — the opposite of passivity or laziness.
verses.prayer: God, help me do my very best for others.
verses.discussion_question: Why is going the extra mile to help others important?
verses.family_discussion: What does it look like in our family to go 'the extra distance' for one another rather than only doing the minimum?
verses.do_it_today: Do more than the minimum for someone today. Go a little further than you have to.
verses.illustration_prompt: A beautiful ship sailing on a wide sea bringing cargo home, cutting through golden waters, warm watercolour with a sense of adventure and purpose

verses.kjv: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.
verses.little_bible: She wakes up while it is still dark. She makes food for her family. She cares for everyone in her home.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She gets up early to care for everyone in her home.
verses.meaning: Rising before dawn reflects extraordinary dedication. She is not sleeping in while others wait. She gives food to her household and assigns tasks to her servants, showing that her leadership begins before the sun rises. Disciplined mornings are a mark of the excellent woman.
verses.prayer: God, help me serve others before myself.
verses.discussion_question: Why is being willing to get up early and serve others a sign of good character?
verses.family_discussion: What morning rhythms do we model as parents that show our children what sacrificial, early service looks like?
verses.do_it_today: Wake up tomorrow and do one helpful thing before you do anything for yourself.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman standing in her kitchen in the pre-dawn darkness, lamplight glowing, preparing food with quiet and purposeful energy, warm watercolour tones

verses.kjv: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.
verses.little_bible: She looks carefully at a field and decides to buy it. She plants a vineyard with the money she has earned.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She plans wisely and plants things that will grow.
verses.meaning: This verse reveals her capacity for wise, long-range planning and enterprise. She is not merely a domestic figure — she evaluates land, makes economic decisions, and invests her earned income in future productivity. The excellent woman is a wise steward of resources and a planner for the future.
verses.prayer: God, help me think ahead and plan wisely.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to think carefully before making a big decision?
verses.family_discussion: How do we involve our children in household planning, budgeting, or planting — teaching them that wisdom includes looking ahead and managing resources well?
verses.do_it_today: Make a simple plan for something you want to do this week. Write down three steps.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman standing at the edge of a field, looking out thoughtfully, a vineyard growing behind her in the golden light, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.
verses.little_bible: She makes herself strong. She is ready to work hard every day.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She keeps herself strong and ready to work.
verses.meaning: To gird the loins meant to prepare for vigorous action — pulling up long robes so that legs were free to move and work. This is physical readiness born of commitment. She does not wait for work to come to her; she prepares her body and her will for the demands of her calling.
verses.prayer: God, make me strong and ready to work.
verses.discussion_question: How do you prepare yourself when you have something important to do?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children that strength is cultivated — that preparation, discipline, and readiness require intentional effort?
verses.do_it_today: Before you start something hard today, take a deep breath, prepare yourself, and do it well.
verses.illustration_prompt: A strong woman rolling up her sleeves with energy and determination, ready to work in the morning light, confident posture, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She perceiveth that her merchandise is good: her candle goeth not out by night.
verses.little_bible: She knows her work is good and valuable. She works late into the night if her family needs her.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She works until the job is done right.
verses.meaning: She has discernment about quality — she knows when her work is good. And her lamp burning through the night reveals her commitment: she does not stop when it is merely convenient to stop. There is no laziness or half-heartedness in her. She works as long as the task requires.
verses.prayer: God, help me finish what I start.
verses.discussion_question: What does it look like to do a job all the way to the end?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop persistence — the willingness to keep going until something is truly done rather than stopping when it gets hard?
verses.do_it_today: Finish one thing you started but have not completed yet.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman working by candlelight late at night, her candle glowing warmly in the darkness, hands busy, focused and peaceful, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.
verses.little_bible: She uses her hands to spin thread. She makes cloth and clothing for her family.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Her hands are always busy making good things.
verses.meaning: The spindle and distaff were the tools for making thread from raw wool or flax — the beginning of the textile process. She is personally engaged in productive craft. She does not outsource what she can do herself. Her hands are creatively and productively at work in the home.
verses.prayer: God, help me use my hands for good.
verses.discussion_question: What good things can your hands make or do?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to see their hands as tools for creation and service — and involve them in making and building real things?
verses.do_it_today: Make something with your hands today. Draw a picture, build something, or help cook.
verses.illustration_prompt: Close-up of skilled hands working at a spinning wheel, turning raw wool into thread, warm lamplight casting gentle shadows, delicate watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.
verses.little_bible: She reaches out to help poor people. She gives to those who are in need.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She always helps people who are poor and need help.
verses.meaning: Her generosity to the poor is sandwiched between her household productivity — showing that caring for her family and caring for the wider community are not opposites. The repetition of 'hand' and 'hands' connects her productive work with her charitable giving: the same hands that spin thread reach out to the poor.
verses.prayer: God, help me give to those who need help.
verses.discussion_question: How can you help someone who has less than you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we make generosity to the poor a rhythm of our household rather than an occasional event?
verses.do_it_today: Find something you can give away to someone who needs it more than you do.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman's hand reaching out warmly to a small, humble figure at her door, gentle light between them, expressions of kindness and gratitude, watercolour

verses.kjv: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household are clothed with scarlet.
verses.little_bible: She is not afraid when winter comes. Her family is warm and well-clothed. She prepared in advance.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She is ready for hard times. Her family is safe.
verses.meaning: Scarlet cloth was thick and warm — the best protection against cold. Her lack of fear is not naivety; it is the confidence that comes from preparation. She has already anticipated difficulty and acted. Wisdom prepares for hard seasons before they arrive.
verses.prayer: God, help me prepare for hard times ahead.
verses.discussion_question: How can preparing in advance protect you when hard times come?
verses.family_discussion: What are we doing as a family to be spiritually, financially, and relationally prepared for hard seasons — not in fear, but in wise anticipation?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one thing that is coming up that might be hard. Make a plan to prepare for it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A mother warmly wrapping her children in thick red cloaks as snow falls outside the window, calm and confident expression, cosy home, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing is silk and purple.
verses.little_bible: She makes beautiful bed coverings. She wears fine and dignified clothing herself.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She takes care of her home and dresses with dignity.
verses.meaning: Purple and silk were marks of dignity and prosperity in the ancient world, attainable because of her diligent work. She does not neglect herself while serving others. She carries herself with dignity. Her personal care flows from her productive life, not from vanity.
verses.prayer: God, help me carry myself with dignity.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between being dignified and being vain?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our daughters to take care of their appearance as an expression of self-respect and dignity — rooted in character, not performance for others?
verses.do_it_today: Take care of yourself today — clean your room, dress neatly, and carry yourself with confidence.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman dressed in rich purple and fine linen, standing with quiet dignity and warmth in her well-kept home, soft watercolour tones of gold and purple

verses.kjv: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.
verses.little_bible: Her husband is respected in the city. He sits with the leaders of the land. Her good name helps him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Her husband is respected because of who she is.
verses.meaning: The gates of the city were where judges, elders, and leaders sat to conduct public affairs. Her husband's good standing in that community is partly the fruit of her faithful character at home. A godly woman lifts those around her — her excellence has public ripple effects.
verses.prayer: God, help me lift the people around me.
verses.discussion_question: How does one person's good character help everyone around them?
verses.family_discussion: How does the character of each family member affect the reputation and flourishing of the whole family — and how do we talk about this with our children?
verses.do_it_today: Do something today that makes your family proud. Be someone who lifts others.
verses.illustration_prompt: A respected man sitting among elders at a city gate, wisdom and dignity in the scene, the warm glow of a thriving city around them, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
verses.little_bible: She makes high-quality linen cloth and sells it. She sells fine belts to traders in the city.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She makes things and sells them with care and skill.
verses.meaning: She is an entrepreneur: she produces goods and trades them in the marketplace. This is not hidden or private — she sells to merchants, engaging the commercial world with skill and integrity. Her domestic excellence extends into economic enterprise. Work and commerce are dignified.
verses.prayer: God, help me do honest and good work.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to do honest work that helps others?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children that commerce, trade, and business can be expressions of godly character and service — not just opportunities for personal gain?
verses.do_it_today: Do one task today with as much care and quality as if you were giving it to someone you love.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman at a market stall, presenting beautiful linen cloth to a merchant with confidence and a warm smile, a busy but orderly marketplace, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
verses.little_bible: Strength and honour are what she is known for. She is not afraid of the future.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She is strong and honourable. She smiles at the future.
verses.meaning: Character is here described as clothing — it is what covers her, defines how she is seen, and protects her. Because she has built her life on faithfulness and integrity, she can face tomorrow without fear. True security is not found in wealth or status but in a life well-lived.
verses.prayer: God, make strength and honour my clothing.
verses.discussion_question: Why is good character better protection than money or looks?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that the character they are building now is the foundation of their future — that what they are inside shapes the life they will have?
verses.do_it_today: Think about what your character looks like right now. Is there something you want to build or change?
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman standing tall in glowing light, her expression calm and courageous as dawn breaks before her, strength and peace in her posture, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.
verses.little_bible: When she speaks, she speaks with wisdom. Her words are always kind.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She speaks wisely and kindly.
verses.meaning: Wisdom and kindness govern her speech — not just occasionally but as a law, a consistent pattern. The 'law of kindness' means kindness is not an exception or a mood; it is her rule. Her tongue is under the direction of both wisdom and love — a rare and powerful combination.
verses.prayer: God, put kind and wise words in my mouth.
verses.discussion_question: How can you make sure your words are both wise and kind?
verses.family_discussion: How do we as parents model a tongue governed by both wisdom and kindness — and how do we correct our children toward this standard rather than merely toward politeness?
verses.do_it_today: Before you speak today, ask yourself: Is this wise? Is this kind? Then say it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman speaking gently to a group of listening children and adults, a glow around her words, peace in the room, warm watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.
verses.little_bible: She watches over everything happening in her home. She never wastes time doing nothing.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: She watches over her home and does not waste time.
verses.meaning: Active oversight of the household is her calling — she pays attention, she manages, she is aware. And she refuses idleness. The 'bread of idleness' is the provision that comes from doing nothing — she has no part in it. Her diligence is both active (oversight) and negative (refusal of laziness).
verses.prayer: God, help me use my time for good.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between resting and being lazy?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand the difference between godly rest and idleness — and what does an ordered, well-managed home teach them about stewardship?
verses.do_it_today: Find one thing that needs doing at home and do it without being asked.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman walking through her home with a watchful and caring eye, everything in good order around her, warm natural light, purposeful expression, watercolour

verses.kjv: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.
verses.little_bible: Her children say she is blessed and wonderful. Her husband praises her too.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Her family loves her and says she is wonderful.
verses.meaning: This is the harvest of her faithful life: spontaneous, genuine praise from the people who know her best. Her children and husband are not strangers — they have seen her day after day. And their verdict is: she is blessed. True legacy is built inside the home, where no audience is watching.
verses.prayer: God, help me live so my family is blessed.
verses.discussion_question: Why does it matter what the people in your own home think of you?
verses.family_discussion: How intentional are we about verbally praising and blessing those in our own household — expressing the love and appreciation we feel rather than assuming they know?
verses.do_it_today: Tell someone in your family something specific you love or appreciate about them.
verses.illustration_prompt: Children hugging their mother with joy and gratitude, a husband nearby with a warm admiring smile, a peaceful and loving home, golden watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.
verses.little_bible: Many women have done excellent and good things. But you are better than all of them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Many are good. But you are the very best.
verses.meaning: The husband's praise reaches its peak: she surpasses all others. This is the language of honour — an extravagant blessing spoken over a faithful woman. It echoes the rarity of verse 10: finding such a woman was precious, and when found, she deserved to be celebrated fully.
verses.prayer: God, help me live with true excellence.
verses.discussion_question: What does it look like to truly excel — not just be okay, but be excellent?
verses.family_discussion: How do we call forth the best from the people in our home — creating an atmosphere where excellence is celebrated, not envied?
verses.do_it_today: Try to do one thing today with real excellence — not just good enough, but your very best.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman crowned not with gold but with a wreath of flowers and light, her family standing around her with joy and celebration, soft glowing watercolour

verses.kjv: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
verses.little_bible: Good looks and charm can be deceiving. They do not last. But a woman who fears the LORD will always be praised.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Looks fade. Fearing God lasts forever.
verses.meaning: This is the theological heart of the entire chapter. Outward favour (charm, social appeal) is deceitful — it lies about a person's true worth. Beauty is vain — it is empty and fleeting. But the fear of the LORD is the foundation of real and lasting praise. This verse ties the entire poem back to the opening of Proverbs: 'the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.'
verses.prayer: God, help me fear You more than looks.
verses.discussion_question: Why does the Bible say beauty can be vain or empty?
verses.family_discussion: How do we speak about beauty and appearance in our home in a way that teaches our children to value the fear of the LORD above all external qualities?
verses.do_it_today: Look in the mirror and remind yourself: what lasts is not how you look, but who you are inside.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman standing in humble dignity before a mirror that shows not her outward face but her glowing inner character and a radiant light of reverence for God, watercolour

verses.kjv: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.
verses.little_bible: Let her receive what her hard work has produced. Let her good works speak for her in public.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Her own good work speaks for her everywhere.
verses.meaning: The chapter closes with a call for public recognition of the excellent woman. The 'gates' — the place of civic life and public honour — are where her works should praise her. This is not boasting; it is justice. Her faithful, diligent, generous life deserves to be seen, celebrated, and rewarded. Let your life be its own testimony.
verses.prayer: God, let my good works glorify You.
verses.discussion_question: What do you want people to say about you because of how you live?
verses.family_discussion: What legacy are we building as a family — what will our 'works' say about us in the community around us, and are we living in a way we would want publicly praised?
verses.do_it_today: Do something good today that you would be happy for anyone to see. Let your works speak.
verses.illustration_prompt: A woman walking with purpose through city gates, the community around her pausing to honour her, her works visible all around — a thriving home, helped neighbours, a planted vineyard — golden watercolour scene
